rationale: Zero-ask approver regression check on b98d06c2 in the decomposition lens: clean, and the round-5 fix moves bead 6 in the RIGHT direction for my lens — the write-ahead marker REPLACES the two-ref transaction, deleting a whole machinery layer (no multi-ref transaction helper, no version floor beyond plain update-ref/commit-tree/read-tree, one marker OID encoding intended tip + predecessor-as-first-parent) while the discriminator becomes total over three structurally-identified states. The diff is confined to the OQ-1 protocol paragraph, the ADR Fitness §2/§3 sentence, and bead 6's steps 1/4/5 + fixture roster; beads 1-5 and 7-10 are untouched; no depends_on changed in any of the six commits; no new file names were introduced (marker/advance helpers stay in internal/gitutil beside recordMergeSourceMarker, fixtures in complete_test.go, the amendment in ADR-0041 + its test) — chunk/section parity holds in its final state. The thirteen-leg count is arithmetically right (legs i-xiii, each individually stated) and the all-legs-on-files-backend pin makes the crash-window legs (xii)/(xiii) actually meaningful. On the lead's question: bead 6 with thirteen fixture legs is still ONE reviewable deliverable, and more reviewably so than last round — the fixture matrix grew by exactly the two one-ref-installed windows the simpler design newly exposes, while the production machinery SHRANK; a bead's reviewability is governed by the mechanism surface its panel must hold in mind, not by its test count, and that surface got smaller. Keep whole, recorded as acceptable-but-large below.

findings.title: Bead 6 final size judgment: acceptable-but-large, keep whole — strengthened by the write-ahead simplification
findings.detail: The round-5 redesign deleted the two-ref transaction helper and its multi-ref-atomicity dependency; per-stage mechanics are now build-object → publish marker → single-ref expected-old advance, with a total three-way re-entry discriminator. Thirteen fixture legs is a large roster, but eleven of them existed last round and the two additions (xii/xiii) each pin exactly one crash window the simpler design has — the matrix is the bead panel's falsification instrument, not added scope. The split candidate remains worse than the whole for the reason recorded in rounds 2-5, now with a sixth round of evidence: every substantive protocol defect this gate found (synthetic artifact deletion, phantom staged deletions, the over-read transaction atomicity, the silent interval-edit loss G2 closed this round) lived in the seam between primitive semantics and consumer expectation, which is precisely the line a primitives/flow split would sever review across. One nit, sub-round grade: the S-stage exit contract cites 'the existing artifact/user classifier' without naming its package home (the artifactPaths classifier lives in internal/next/guard.go); bead 6 only CONSUMES it, so no chunk entry is owed, but the implementer will need to confirm the import direction (internal/complete -> internal/next) introduces no cycle or else re-host the classifier — a plan-text pointer would have cost one clause. Not blocking: consumption-not-modification, and the bead's own build gate surfaces any cycle immediately.
